items.article_search_text: The McLaren boss attributes the Australian's lack of pace to excessive reflection behind the wheel of the MCL40. The team has designed a plan for him to recover his fluency and fight for the podium again in the final stretch of the season. Andrea Stella has identified the source of Oscar Piastri [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/oscar-piastri-describes-spanish-gp-as-painful-after-challenging-f1-outing]'s problems. The McLaren boss considers that the Australian driver is "thinking too much" while driving the MCL40, which prevents him from extracting the full potential of the car and is costing him valuable tenths in qualifying and races: "I think with Oscar we need to qualify better and be closer to the podium positions from the start, there are several circumstances over which we need more control. We need to execute the work better and at the same time achieve greater synchrony between Oscar and the MCL40, since he still drives thinking too much" declared Stella in Madrid. The Italian executive's diagnosis points to an adaptation problem. Piastri, who in 2025 had stood out for his ability to maintain great speed in fast corners, has not been able to consistently reproduce that style with the current generation of cars, the reduction in downforce and narrower tires have altered the behavior of the cars, reducing available grip and demanding a different driving approach. Oscar Piastri describes Spanish GP as “painful” after challenging F1 outing [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/60f26e36-1416-4168-8752-9508c5914746.jpeg] Oscar Piastri describes Spanish GP as “painful” after challenging F1 outing The Australian finished eighth after suffering front wing damage on the first lap from contact with Russell. The bad timing of the Virtual Safety Car and a complicated qualifying session hampered his race at Madring. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/oscar-piastri-describes-spanish-gp-as-painful-after-challenging-f1-outing] For Piastri that adaptation process is proving slower than expected, Stella explained how this excess reflection directly affects performance: "When you drive thinking too much everything becomes slower, you become slower as a driver when deciding what to do and consequently, you do slower laps" he noted. The McLaren [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/mclaren]boss trusts that the team can reverse the situation. "The plan is very clear in terms of what we need to improve and I hope we get past this seeing a stronger Piastri in the final part of the year" he added. The Monza case is a representative example of Piastri's season, the Australian qualified third but a penalty for impeding another driver dropped him to sixth place on the grid, ruining his podium chances: "In Monza, he was third in qualifying but we ended up starting sixth due to a penalty. There are several circumstances over which we need more control" lamented Stella. F1 Stock Watch: Who Gained and Lost More After Madrid? [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/b429bb20-8779-402e-811d-c0b69c9373bc.jpeg] F1 Stock Watch: Who Gained and Lost More After Madrid? Kimi Antonelli's stock is through the roof, while Carlos Sainz Jr's hometown flop will hurt him. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/f1-stock-watch-who-gained-and-lost-more-after-madrid] The figures reflect the gap between McLaren's two drivers, Piastri has 120 points and occupies seventh place in the championship, with two podiums and no wins. Lando Norris, for his part, is fourth with 186 points, two wins and five podiums. The 66 point difference between them is a reflection of the Australian's lack of consistency, who has not managed to find the consistency needed to fight for the title. McLaren has established a strategy to recover Piastri's performance in the second half of the season. The goal is to achieve greater synchrony between the driver and the car so that Piastri can drive more instinctively and less analytically, the team trusts that with more adaptation time and specific work on the MCL40's setup, the Australian can recover the fluency that led him to shine in previous seasons. Formula 1 [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1] will return to action in Baku, where Piastri will have a new opportunity to demonstrate that McLaren's recovery plan is producing results. The Australian knows time is pressing and that every race is a chance to recover the confidence and pace that made him one of the most promising drivers on the grid.

Former Haas Formula 1 driver Romain Grosjean has apologised to Zak Brown after "misunderstanding" Brown's comments on Oscar Piastri in Madrid . Grosjean attended the Spanish GP as a pundit for French television station Canal+ alongside appearing on F1 TV . The ex-F1 driver was in screen during an F1 TV interview with McLaren boss Zak Brown after qualifying at the Madring where Lando Norris took pole position. Oscar Piastri qualified in P7, four tenths behind his teammate. “I think you’ve got Lando on his A-plus game, so I don’t think there was anything left lap-time-wise there and so he found that," Brown said. “Oscar has been right there with him all weekend and just didn’t get that same extra [performance] that lap. “We’ll continue to look at it. He’ll look at the data and probably do what we all did and go: ‘Wow, what a lap!” Oscar Piastri did not have a successful race at the Madring Grosjean admits to Zak Brown misunderstanding on Oscar Piastri remarks During his Spanish GP commentary with Canal+ the next day, Grosjean claimed that Brown had been heavily critical of Piastri, adding that Brown had said Norris is a world champion and better driver than Piastri. On Sunday evening, Grosjean posted an apology to social media, admitting that he had misinterpreted the McLaren boss' words. The post read: “Today, I made a comment on Canal Plus F1 regarding Zak Brown’s comments about Oscar Piastri during an interview yesterday on F1 TV, which I was part of. “I completely misunderstood his words and want to apologise for that. I know how important it is to Zak and the entire McLaren team to respect their drivers and treat them fairly and equally. “McLaren had the fastest car today and were unlucky with the VSC. I’m sure both Lando and Oscar will have another chance to fight for the win in Baku.” Unfortunate Virtual Safety Car timing and a long pit stop deprived Norris and McLaren of a win in Madrid, with the reigning World Champion eventually finishing third. items.article_search_text: The Australian finished eighth after suffering front wing damage on the first lap from contact with Russell. The bad timing of the Virtual Safety Car and a complicated qualifying session hampered his race at Madring. Oscar Piastri lived a real ordeal at the Spanish Grand Prix. The Australian McLaren [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/mclaren] driver, who arrived in Madrid hoping to score important points, was forced to settle for eighth position after a race marked by damage to his car and a series of adverse circumstances that prevented him from showing his true potential. The problem began on the first lap, Piastri was involved in an incident with George Russell [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/tyre-overheating-cost-george-russell-in-madrid-mercedes-driver-reveals] when the Briton's Mercedes crossed into his path toward the barriers, the Australian had nowhere to go and suffered damage to his front wing, specifically the endplate, which made him lose downforce for the rest of the race, the team was able to mitigate the problem at his only pit stop, but not fully solve it. "It was quite painful, obviously, from lap 1, there wasn't much I could do from there" declared Piastri after the race. The Australian also pointed to the bad luck with the timing of the Virtual Safety Car: "The VSC timing certainly wasn't ideal for us, we stayed on the hards and it was a difficult afternoon" he explained. F1 Spanish Grand Prix: Antonelli Takes Victory in an Uneventful Madrid Race [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/bd727c6d-9645-49e9-8c31-d602dfb11e57.jpeg] F1 Spanish Grand Prix: Antonelli Takes Victory in an Uneventful Madrid Race Kimi Antonelli extends his championship lead with a patient and calculated race in the Spanish Grand Prix. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/f1-spanish-grand-prix-antonelli-takes-victory-in-an-uneventful-madrid-race] Piastri had chosen not to pit under the VSC, betting on a long stint strategy in the hope of a later Safety Car or red flag. However, there were no further incidents and he was forced to make his stop in race conditions, which made him lose time and come out in traffic. Although he managed an overtake on Arvid Lindblad, one of the few of the day, he could not get past Franco Colapinto's Alpine in the final laps. To understand Piastri's difficulties, you have to go back to Saturday's qualifying, the Australian needed an extra set of soft tires to secure his place in Q2, which left him as the only front running driver with a used set of the C4 compound for his first Q3 lap. On his second attempt with new tires he made a mistake at the start of the lap and could only qualify seventh, which left him in the middle of the pack, an always dangerous position at the narrow first corner of Madring. F1 Daily: A Chaotic F3 Crash at Madrid, Norris's Super Lap, and Sainz's Penalty [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/f26232b4-2d99-4e67-b08a-f14b8d25572f.jpeg] F1 Daily: A Chaotic F3 Crash at Madrid, Norris's Super Lap, and Sainz's Penalty A chaotic crash at a Formula 3 race started things off the wrong way at the Madring. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/f1-daily-a-chaotic-f3-crash-at-madrid-norriss-super-lap-and-sainzs-penalty] "It was mainly the end of qualifying and then lap 1, obviously it was far from ideal, with damage throughout the race, it was hard like that, but today we tried to learn as much as possible to get more out of the car and out of my driving, hopefully we have learned some things for the rest of the year" summarized Piastri. The 2026 season is being a constant contrast for Piastri. While his teammate Lando Norris accumulates five podiums, two wins, three poles and a Sprint win, the Australian has only two podiums, the last in Miami and a third place in a Sprint. In the championship, Norris is 66 points ahead of him, a difference that reflects Piastri's difficulty in finding consistency. The Australian hopes his luck will change soon. The next round in Baku in two weeks gives him a chance for redemption. Last year Azerbaijan was the scene where his championship hopes suffered a hard blow after an early retirement, something Piastri will want to make up for when the Formula 1 paddock gathers again on the streets of the Azerbaijani capital.

Oscar Piastri received a black-and-white flag from the FIA during Sunday's Spanish Grand Prix for exceeding track limits, and admitted afterwards that he'd overstepped. The McLaren driver was carrying front-wing damage after first-lap contact with George Russell's Mercedes, which affected the car for the rest of the race. He finished eighth, his worst result since 11th in Canada. Piastri said the contact happened when Russell kept squeezing him toward the wall. He braked to avoid him, and both cars ended up bunched together. He said it was "easy to go a little bit too far" on a track with no kerb or wall on the inside of some corners. "It was just a tough afternoon from literally the start,” Piastri reflected to the media, including Motorsport Week . "From then on, the rest of the race was very compromised, obviously with some of the damage and the track position mainly.” "I was alongside, and he just kept squeezing me to the wall, and then I hit the brakes and kind of avoided him. But amongst all that, he hit the brakes as well. Everyone hit the brakes, and we kind of got stuck together and everything.” "I was just expecting a bit more space, and obviously between a car and a wall, you can't make any more space, so that was tricky.” "On a track like this, you're always searching for a bit of clean air in the high-speed corners, and with no kerb or wall on the inside of some of the corners, it's very easy to just go a little bit too far." Despite the finish, Piastri felt he'd had a decent race in clean air, but said getting stuck behind a train of cars after the pit stops, including Franco Colapinto's Alpine, cost him further. He said the medium tyre was good for one lap and then fell away badly. "I think the pace and clean air on the hard was pretty good, but we were trying to make up the pit loss of the VSC to the guys who pitted, and once they got the loss back, I was stuck again, so that was painful," said Piastri. "Then when we pitted onto the medium, we pitted into a four-car train, and that wasn't great, and the medium tyre was just awful. "It was good for [one lap], and then it was pretty terrible, so a lot of things to try and fix."

items.article_search_text: Romain Grosjean a présenté ses excuses à Zak Brown après avoir reconnu avoir mal interprété les déclarations du CEO de McLaren. Le Français avait affirmé à l’antenne de Canal+ que Brown avait sévèrement critiqué l’Australien après les qualifications du Grand Prix d’Espagne, alors que ses propos étaient en réalité beaucoup plus mesurés. Présent au Madring dans son rôle de consultant pour Canal+ et intervenant également sur F1 TV, Grosjean s’est retrouvé au cœur d’un malentendu concernant Zak Brown et Oscar Piastri. Norris mieux que Piastri L’ancien pilote Lotus et Haas avait participé samedi à une séquence de F1 TV au cours de laquelle Brown avait été interrogé après les qualifications. Lando Norris venait alors de décrocher la pole position, tandis que son équipier Piastri avait dû se contenter de la septième place, à quatre dixièmes du Britannique. Interrogé sur ce qui avait manqué à Piastri pour rivaliser avec son équipier, Brown avait avant tout insisté sur la qualité exceptionnelle du tour réalisé par Norris : « Je pense que Lando était à son meilleur niveau, donc je ne crois pas qu’il restait quoi que ce soit à aller chercher en termes de chrono. Et pourtant, il l’a trouvé », expliquait le dirigeant américain. Brown soulignait également que Piastri avait été proche de Norris pendant le reste du week-end, mais qu’il n’était simplement pas parvenu à trouver le même supplément de performance au moment décisif : « Oscar était juste à côté de lui tout le week-end, mais il n’a simplement pas trouvé ce même petit plus sur ce tour. » Le patron de McLaren ajoutait que l’équipe analyserait les données et que Piastri lui-même pourrait surtout constater à quel point le tour de Norris avait été réussi : « Il regardera probablement les données et fera comme nous tous : “Waouh, quel tour !” » Grosjean reconnaît avoir mal compris Brown Le lendemain, pendant le Grand Prix, Grosjean est revenu sur cet entretien dans ses commentaires pour Canal+. Le Français a alors présenté les déclarations de Brown d’une manière beaucoup plus sévère, affirmant notamment que le dirigeant de McLaren avait passé la performance de Piastri « à la tronçonneuse ». Grosjean a également indiqué que Brown aurait justifié l’écart entre ses pilotes en expliquant que Norris était champion du monde et simplement meilleur que Piastri. Or, ce n’est pas ce que Brown avait déclaré lors de l’entretien. Quelques heures après la course, Grosjean a donc publié un message sur les réseaux sociaux afin de reconnaître son erreur et de présenter humblement ses excuses : « Aujourd’hui, j’ai fait un commentaire sur Canal+ F1 concernant les déclarations de Zak Brown à propos d’Oscar Piastri lors d’une interview hier sur F1 TV, à laquelle je participais. J’ai complètement mal compris ses propos et je tiens à m’en excuser. » Grosjean a ainsi rapidement rectifié ses déclarations, reconnaissant qu’il avait attribué à Brown une comparaison beaucoup plus sévère entre Norris et Piastri que celle réellement formulée par le patron de McLaren. items.article_search_text: No one was happy and even the winner admitted he didn’t deserve to win after some ‘insanely unlucky’ drama. 7NEWS brings you the latest local news from Australia and around the world. Stay up to date with all of the breaking sport, politics, entertainment, finance, weather and business headlines. Today's news, live updates & all the latest breaking stories from 7NEWS. Wonder boy Kimi Antonelli has roared ever closer to the world Formula 1 crown with victory around the new Madrid street circuit — but there was nothing but gloom for McLaren as Lando Norris got “insanely unlucky” and Oscar Piastri’s wretched season continued with an eighth-place finish in a damaged car. Antonelli took another huge stride towards becoming the youngest world champion ever with his Spanish Grand Prix victory, but even the 20-year-old was happy to concede he had got seriously fortunate on Sunday (Monday AEST) to oust third-placed Norris. “I feel a bit bad for Lando, he deserved to win,” shrugged Antonelli, after he took full advantage of Lance Stroll putting his Aston Martin in the wall on the 14th lap to earn a free pit-stop during a Virtual Safety Car period. Meanwhile, world champion Norris, who’d been looking unstoppable seven seconds ahead at the front, had just passed the pit entry, and missed a chance of a cheap tyre change. Piastri was not even really at the races once his McLaren collided twice on the opening lap with George Russell’s Mercedes, and he ended up having to battle through the race with a damaged front wing. McLaren decided not to change it because time would be lost but just altered the angle to provide more downforce when a disgruntled-sounding Piastri eventually pitted on lap 42. Emerging in 11th place, he fought to get back among the points but it will still dismay him to end up a minute-and-a-half slower than his teammate. “It was pretty painful, obviously from lap one,” sighed Piastri, who reckoned the real damage had come by finishing seventh in qualifying. “Not much I really could have done from that first lap, having damage for the whole race. It was just a difficult afternoon.” Norris dropped to fifth after a slow front-right tyre change when he did stop under the VSC and could only make up two places on the new Madring circuit where overtaking is at a premium. “I don’t know how someone looks at this design and goes, mint!” Norris said. Audi driver Gabriel Bortoleto added: “I almost fell asleep.” Fernando Alonso said it was “sad” that the key feature of the track — the banked Monumental corner — was so easy in these cars his Aston Martin team press officer could drive it flat-out. All the drivers rued the lack of overtaking opportunities and hoped for layout changes, particularly with the turn 5-6 chicane, before the next visit in 2027. Beyond the entertainment of it all Carlos Sainz also said there was little thought to driver safety. The Madring follows the fast but walled street circuit template put forward by Baku, Jeddah and Las Vegas in more recent years. “It seems like the FIA is happy to go in this direction moving forward in terms of new circuits, which obviously, as drivers, we are raising our, not concerns, but our point of wanting to keep improving safety,” the Williams driver said. “We’re going to go towards these circuits because going at 260km/h, 270km/h on esses that you cannot see through is definitely eye-opening and definitely makes you question how safe everything is.” Despite his superior pace in the first race to be held in Madrid for 45 years prompting team boss Zak Brown to say he’d been in “a league of his own”, Norris couldn’t pass Max Verstappen for second, even though he felt the Dutchman had illegally run off the road while defending his position on the penultimate lap. So Verstappen finished runner-up, 4.3sec behind the Italian winner, with polesitter Norris third just seven-tenths back. “Insanely unlucky with the Virtual Safety Car ... I was the only once who didn’t get a chance to do the pit stop there. Of course I feel like I deserved more,” Norris sighed, before suggesting the lottery of pitting under the VSC needed to be changed. Charles Leclerc was fourth, and Russell fifth as Antonelli extended his advantage in the championship race with an eighth win of the year to 81 points with nine rounds remaining. Lewis Hamilton’s fading championship hopes also suffered further when he retired early on with a brake problem. He’s now 101 points behind Antonelli, 20 behind Russell and five ahead of fourth-placed Norris. Charles Leclerc is fifth, Verstappen sixth and Piastri seventh, now a whopping 172 points off the lead. — with 7NEWS Journalist from Australian news agency, Australian Associated Press.
